title: GoldenRetrievalBenchmarkCaseSchemaV2
description: Gate 3 Step 16 benchmark. Extends the v1 case schema with an expectation review (verdict A-E/VALID plus the evidence behind it) and the stable physical identity of every expected metric and dimension. v1 cases and their expectations are carried through byte-for-byte; nothing in `expected` is altered by this schema.

expectation_review.description: Step 16 triage. Exactly one verdict per case, with the evidence that produced it.

verdict.description: A = software defect (expectation is achievable under current configuration but the system does not meet it). B = outdated or incorrect benchmark expectation. C = database/data limitation. D = intentionally unsupported capability. E = genuine ambiguity requiring a human/business decision. VALID = expectation verified against live configuration and currently met.

verdict_meaning.description: Plain-language expansion of the verdict letter, so the file is readable without the schema.

rationale.description: Why this verdict and not another.

evidence.description: What the verdict was derived from. config_problems is empty when every expected metric, dimension and value exists and is usable.

config_problems.description: Each expectation that cannot be met under live configuration.

diagnostic_run.description: Result of executing the case during Step 16 triage. Diagnostic only - this is NOT the Step 14 accuracy baseline.

original_expected.description: The v1 expectation, copied verbatim for historical comparison. Never modified.

recommended_expected.description: Proposed replacement expectation for verdict B, where a single correct value is evidenced. Null otherwise. This is a RECOMMENDATION - it is not applied to `expected` in this step.

requires_human_review.description: True when the correct expectation is a business decision rather than a mechanical correction.

expectation_changed_in_v2.description: Whether `expected` differs from v1. Step 16 leaves this false for every case: verdicts and recommendations are recorded, no expectation is rewritten.

expected_identity.description: Stable physical identity for each expected metric and dimension, resolved from live configuration. Business names are display strings an administrator may rename at any time; (table_name, column_name) is what a rename cannot break. Recorded alongside the names rather than replacing them, so v1 and v2 stay comparable.

resolved.description: False when no active, non-excluded row carries this business name.

ambiguous_across_tables.description: True when the same business name is configured on more than one table, so the name alone cannot identify the column.
